bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR in ApiServer.GetUserRoles (gRPC/HTTP /api/v1/GetUserRoles): after authenticating the caller via GetUserFromContext, the handler trusted user-supplied UserRequest.Name and UserRequest.Org with no READ_RESULTS or ORG_ADMIN check, loaded that org's config, and returned the target user's ACL policy (roles, permissions, effective permissions) for any org. Any authenticated low-privilege user who already knew a target username and org id could enumerate ACL policies across organizations.
flaw_origin: PR #2212 originally added GetUserRoles with a users.GetUser(principal, in.Name) PermissionDenied gate and iterated only that user's orgs. Member 90208c6d9d29b64333ad2667285b1a9c39c6d72e (Mike Cohen, 'Reworked the user management GUI') discarded that gate, discarded the unused principal, and rewrote the handler to GetOrgConfig(in.Org) plus acl_manager.GetPolicy(org, in.Name) under the comment 'Allow the user to ask about other orgs.' That rewrite is the first write of the IDOR. GitHub squash-merged the PR to master as 7ee677176c05df346baaa39769cd31f7b9f8c66b; GetUserRoles at the squash equals the 90208c6 body. The check stayed absent until PR #4795.

reasoning: CVE-2026-7573 is a published Rapid7 advisory (not withdrawn) for an authorization bypass in GetUserRoles: any authenticated user could supply Name and Org and read another user's ACL in another org. The endpoint was added in PR #2212 member 6d785ec with a users.GetUser visibility check. The IDOR itself is the later rewrite in 90208c6 that dropped that check and bound policy lookup to caller-controlled Org/Name. Parent 20dabe0 still has the GetUser gate, so 90208c6 is the smallest first-write of the flawed mechanism. Master squash 7ee6771 of #2212 is not the BIC; its GetUserRoles text matches 90208c6 exactly and no later PR member retouched the function. The check was restored on master by 2b0ea2d / squash 3c84e64 (PR #4795) with READ_RESULTS plus ORG_ADMIN, and cherry-picked to the 0.76 line as a79bb66, which is in v0.76.4+ while v0.76.2 remains vulnerable, consistent with the advisory's <0.76.5 patched boundary (0.76.5 is a binary under GitHub release v0.76; git has no v0.76.5 tag). AI attribution is from the BIC object only: human maintainer Mike Cohen, no AI/bot trailers, so NOT_AI.
